constructions.title: Yearly median surface Si:DIN ratio

tests.K1_si_din_molar_surface.*.median.is: For one calendar year (the `*` key, taken from the first four characters of `Startdato`), the median molar ratio $\dfrac{\mathrm{Si}/M_{\mathrm{Si}}}{(\mathrm{NO_x} + \mathrm{NH_4})/M_{\mathrm{N}}}$, with $M$ the molar masses (in the code `(si / MM["si"]) / ((nox + nh4) / MM["n"])`). It is taken over station-date-depth cells with depth `dep <= 10` metres that carry silicate (`Silicium`, `µg/l`) and nitrite+nitrate (`Nitrit+nitrat-N`, `µg/l`). Ammonium (`Ammoniak+ammonium-N`) is added when present and taken as zero when absent, and both silicate and DIN must be positive. The median is the element at index `len(v) // 2` of the sorted values, so for an even count it is the upper middle value. Censored results, depth-integrated samples, the depth sentinel `99` and wrong-unit rows are excluded, as are years with fewer cells than the script's minimum. One cell is one station, date and depth rounded to a decimetre, so a station's several shallow depths on one day are separate cells.

constructions.what: After an availability matrix for the hypotheses that were blocked on the water-chemistry fetch, the script computes, for hypothesis `K1` (silicon depletion and the diatom-to-flagellate shift in `docs/HYPOTHESES.md`), the yearly distribution of the surface molar Si:DIN ratio: its median and its share below one. It computes only the nutrient driver; the phytoplankton-community response it is meant to drive is not held.
constructions.model: Water-chemistry rows are kept when `Parameter` matches one of the exact strings in `P` with the unit `P` requires, `ResultatAttribut` is not `<` or `>`, the sample type is `Enkeltprøve` or `Blandingsprøve`, the result and depth parse, the date has `YYYYMMDD` form, and the depth is not the sentinel `99`. Each kept value is written into a dictionary keyed by station, date and depth rounded to one decimal; if a parameter appears more than once in a cell, the last row read wins. In `run_tests`, cells deeper than `10` metres, or lacking silicate or nitrite+nitrate, are skipped. DIN is `nox + (nh4 or 0.0)`, and cells where DIN or silicate is not positive are skipped. Each concentration in micrograms of element per litre is divided by that element's molar mass (`MM`) and the ratio is taken. Ratios are grouped by the year string, sorted, and the value at index `len(v) // 2` is reported, rounded, for each year with at least the minimum cell count.
assumptions: `Silicium` is reported as micrograms of the silicon element per litre, not as silicate or silicon dioxide. The code's comment asserts this for all parameters; it is not checked against a document.

Silicate, nitrite+nitrate and ammonium values in one cell refer to the same fraction (dissolved), although rows are not filtered on `Prøvefraktion` and the extract carries total, dissolved and particulate fractions.
A missing ammonium value means ammonium was negligible, not that it was unmeasured or below detection.
Dropping censored results does not bias the yearly median. Censoring removes exactly the cells where silicate or DIN is depleted, and in opposite directions for the two.

A median pooled over all seasons, stations and depths down to `10` metres represents the year's surface ratio, even though the stations sampled, the months sampled and the number of depths per station change from year to year.
Si:DIN, rather than Si to total nitrogen, is the ratio the hypothesis concerns.

justified.text: The hypothesis names the silicon-to-nitrogen ratio through time as one half of what discriminates it, and silicate as available in the ODA record.
The triage that blocked `K1` on this fetch states the hypothesis in terms of Si:DIN.
Parameter strings and units are taken from the enum sweep, and the unit is enforced per row, because several parameters appear under more than one unit.
Rows are dropped on unit, censoring, sample type, unparseable values and the depth sentinel before any cell is formed.
Censored rows are excluded because a detection limit read as a value biases the parameter high.
The ratio is molar, using element molar masses on concentrations reported as the element.
The ratio, the depth cut, the treatment of ammonium and the median index are exactly as described.

gaps: Although the field sits under `tests`, it is not a test. There is no null, no uncertainty, and no control for station, season or depth, while the script's docstring promises only tests whose null is computable (`scripts/rescore.py:17-19`). The persistence-aware null worked out in `docs/hypodrafts/K1.md` is not applied.

The project's own `K1` design specifies the preceding January-February (pre-bloom) median surface Si:DIN as the quantity that matters, and warns that low silicon beside many diatoms is drawdown, not limitation (`docs/hypodrafts/K1.md`, under The observable consequence and Direction). This median pools all months, so it mixes pre-bloom pools with bloom drawdown.

Station composition changes across years, and the same draft notes that any across-year statistic on pooled medians is partly a statistic about who sampled (`docs/hypodrafts/K1.md`, under The null). Here there are no station fixed effects and no balanced panel.

Rows are not filtered on `Prøvefraktion`, and when a parameter has more than one row in a cell the last one read silently wins. A total and a dissolved silicate value, for example, are not distinguished.
Ammonium absent from a cell is treated as zero, which raises the ratio for that cell. Ammonium is reported on fewer rows than nitrite+nitrate (`counts.nh4.n` against `counts.nox.n`).
Silicate being reported as the element is asserted in a code comment, not documented.

Excluding censored values removes the low-silicate cells that are the very condition `K1` is about, and also the low-DIN cells. The net bias is unquantified and can drift as detection limits and DIN levels change.
Here `surface` means the top `10` metres, while `scripts/cycles.py` uses `MAX_DEPTH`. The same word names two different layers across the site.

The silicon-limitation threshold of one, used for the companion `share_below_1` and in the prose around these medians, rests on the unsourced statement in `docs/HYPOTHESES.md` (hypothesis `K2`) about the silicon-to-nitrogen ratio diatoms require.
The latest calendar year in the output is partial (the extract runs to its fetch date), so its median is taken over an unbalanced part of the season.

The draft keeps the policy-shock reading only as a conditional: if nitrogen fell under management and silicon has no human source, a rise in Si:DIN would be a change in the driver. Neither premise is established on the page, so a rise is not shown to be exogenous to diatoms.
void_if: A year's cells are dominated by one season, a few stations or one area. This applies especially to the latest, partial year.
Some laboratories or periods report `Silicium` as silicate or silicon dioxide, or report a different fraction, under the same parameter string and unit.
Ammonium reporting or detection limits change over time enough to move which cells lose ammonium or are censored.
The extract is re-fetched, or `P`, the depth cut or the minimum cell count changes, and the script is not re-run.
constructions.licenses: A descriptive statement about the archived bottle samples: in the top `10` metres, the pooled yearly median molar Si:DIN in this extract is higher in recent years than in the mid-eighties. That is a first look at the direction of `K1`'s driver, consistent with DIN having fallen while silicon did not.
constructions.not_licensed: Anything about diatoms, flagellates or community composition, which is the response half of `K1` and is not held. That the change is statistically established, monotonic, or true at any particular station or water body. That silicon limitation no longer occurs in any season, the pre-bloom winter pool in particular. That nitrogen management caused the rise. That the premise of `K1` is refuted as a mechanism rather than weakened as a trend.
